### 1 — Scene
A breakfast plate with scrambled eggs, what appears to be scrambled egg whites with reddish sauce, roasted potatoes, grapes, and watermelon. The white food’s identity is somewhat uncertain.

### 2 — Vessel
A large, rounded-square dinner plate, approximately **27 cm across**. Using the requested circular approximation:  
**Area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ 572 cm².** The other plate at the edge is excluded.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area percentages represent separate visible footprints; sauce-covered areas are assigned to sauce rather than counted twice.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |

| Yellow scrambled eggs | 10% | 57 × 1.7 = 97 ml | 0.9 | 87 | 155 | 135 |
| Scrambled egg whites, presumed | 29% | 166 × 1.3 = 216 ml | 0.9 | 194 | 60 | 116 |
| Red grapes | 12% | 69 × 2.0 = 138 ml | 0.65 | 90 | 69 | 62 |

| Roasted potatoes with vegetables | 18% | 103 × 1.5 = 155 ml | 0.65 | 101 | 150 | 152 |
| Reddish sauce, likely salsa | 7% | 40 × 0.8 = 32 ml | 1.0 | 32 | 40 | 13 |

The potatoes’ energy estimate includes cooking oil; no separately measurable pool of oil is visible.

### 8 — Sanity check
The footprints total **86%** of the plate, consistent with the substantial coverage shown. The estimate is **556 g and approximately 494 kcal**—plausible for a full breakfast plate with considerable fruit and egg whites. The white food’s identity and cooking fat are the largest uncertainties.
